title: Pilot Sprint 4 - Concurrency Scrub and Queueing Review
next_steps: Redwood to share updated batching config and perf dashboard by 2027-10-23
Customer to run 24h load test on staging using new concurrency targets and share logs by 2027-10-27
Schedule canary for dedicated pool if 24h test stable - tentative 2027-11-01
action_items: Carlos Mendez: export per-instance KV cache hit heatmap; due 2027-10-23
Aisha Malik: run 24h staging workload with new batching settings; due 2027-10-27
Jamie Huang: share pricing delta for dedicated vs hosted fallback for burst; due 2027-10-24
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on throughput tuning: Redwood reviewed last 48h throughput profile after enabling continuous batching and a modest concurrency raise. Customer reported improved tail latency for short prompts but saw an intermittent surge in queue depth during bursts. Agreed: Redwood to provide finer-grained KV cache telemetry and new batching profile; customer to run 24h staging test and validate fallthrough behavior.
transcript:
Header: Date: 2027-10-21 10:00 PDT | Duration: 46m | Recording Id: ff-20271021-4f9b
Attendees: Jamie H., Carlos M., Priya R. (Redwood) — Aisha M., Tom B., Leah K. (Constella)
[00:00] Jamie Huang: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda: 10m throughput recap, 20m tuning deep dive, 10m next steps. any updates on blockers?
[00:22] Aisha Malik: yeah thanks Jamie. um we ran the two-hour burst test this morning, basically mimicked the card-issuance spikes — saw about a 18% bump in sustained throughput with continuous batching on but, there was like, a spike in queue depth at minute 37 that caused some returns to timeouts.
[00:39] Carlos Mendez: okay that's helpful, can you send the runbook and the raw traces? we suspect that's where the prefix cache miss coincided with a concurrency bump.
[00:50] Tom Bowers: yea we'll send logs. note our staging has slightly different instance sizes so numbers are directional.
[01:02] Priya Rao: quick question — are you on the hosted plan or the dedicated bucket for this test?
[01:08] Aisha Malik: still hosted, we haven't moved to Dedicated yet — wanted to validate configs first, cost concessions etc.
[01:14] Jamie Huang: got it. so todays' numbers — Carlos, you wanna run through the dashboard?
[01:20] Carlos Mendez: sure. slide: last 48h, continuous batching enabled with target latency cap 120ms for tail for short prompts. average tokens/sec increased from 2100 to 2500, so about +19%. median latency actually improved by ~12ms. however, p95 jumped in that one burst window to around 780ms.
[01:46] Leah Kim: p95 780ms — that's above our SLO for auth flows (500ms). is that from the KV cache misses?
[01:52] Carlos Mendez: mostly. we saw a correlated drop in per-shard KV hit rate at the exact time. sometimes the cache warmup + a concurrency ramp can create a transient backpressure.
[02:05] Aisha Malik: hmm the bursts are consumer-driven, unpredictable. we care about steady throughput but also that those spikes don't cause user-visible errors.
[02:12] Jamie Huang: yeah this is the classic latency vs cost tradeoff. continuous batching gives you higher amortized throughput but if a cache-miss storm lines up with a burst, you see queue growth.
[02:24] Speaker 1: (murmur) mm-hmm
[02:28] Carlos Mendez: propose mitigation path: 1) soft concurrency ceiling for the hosted pool (reduce from 48 to 36 per node), 2) modified batching profile that caps max batch size for requests flagged as low-latency, 3) backup fallthrough to a slightly smaller model variant during KV-thrash windows.
[02:51] Tom Bowers: smaller model variant - what's the quality delta there? we can't afford regressions for fraud detection prompts.
[02:57] Priya Rao: we can do A/B evals — small model for short context and for non-critical paths; the runtime will only fallthrough when queue depth exceeds X and tail latency breaches Y. quality delta is usually small on constrained tasks but we will run evals against your prompt set.
[03:19] Aisha Malik: can we see an example of the fallthrough policy? like exact thresholds?
[03:23] Carlos Mendez: yeah I'll include the proposed thresholds in the config dump. offhand we'd set queue depth threshold at 200 requests, p95>600ms sustained for 30s, then trigger fallthrough. but it's tunable.
[03:37] Leah Kim: how does dedicated change this — if we moved to Dedicated reserved pool would we avoid the KV contention?
[03:44] Jamie Huang: Dedicated gives you isolated capacity so you remove noisy neighbor issues and we can tune shard allocation to your traffic distribution. but KV cache is still per-instance; dedicated helps by reducing cross-tenant eviction but doesn't eliminate cold starts.
[03:58] Aisha Malik: pricewise what's the delta for a dedicated pool sized for our peak? ballpark.
[04:03] Jamie Huang: I can share a detailed pricing delta after this call. rough: dedicated committed capacity is typically 20-30% higher cost than hosted at small scale but yields predictable latency and throughput — savings come from fewer fallback invocations and the ability to run more aggressive caching/quantization.
[04:20] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[04:24] Tom Bowers: one more infra note: our staging uses X larger vCPUs and the test generated CPU-bound moments on the host; could that mismatch explain the KV misses?
[04:33] Carlos Mendez: possibly, yes. if instance memory pressure causes more frequent eviction it will look like cache misses. need per-instance mem and eviction metrics.
[04:41] Aisha Malik: we'll add those to the logs.
[04:44] Jamie Huang: ok turning to tuning specifics: continuous batching params we changed were - max_batch_size from 128 -> 160, batch_wait_ms from 12 -> 8, and we enabled prefix-KV affinity to keep keys colocated more often. that explains the throughput bump.
[05:03] Leah Kim: the batch_wait reduction — does that increase queuing? thought shorter waits reduce latency but can hurt throughput if you starve batches?
[05:11] Carlos Mendez: correct, it's a balance. we shortened wait to favor latency for short prompts but increased max_batch_size to recoup throughput. in practice we saw higher throughput with slightly tighter latency for median, but risk on edge cases.
[05:26] Aisha Malik: the one problematic window did align with a background daily job in staging that flushed a lot of keys. bad timing.
[05:33] Jamie Huang: on the diag side, Carlos will produce a heatmap of KV hits over time so we can see eviction waves.
[05:40] Carlos Mendez: yep. also sending a suggested 'auto-throttle' config: if cache hit rate drops below 70% AND queue depth grows by 30% within a minute, throttle new arrivals to the safe concurrency level and spin up burst nodes if available.
[05:54] Tom Bowers: spinning up burst nodes — is that autoscale on Redwood Dedicated? how fast?
[05:59] Priya Rao: burst capacity can be configured for hosted and dedicated. for hosted it's typically a cold spin-up 2-3 minutes depending on region; for dedicated we can pre-warm a small pool so it's near-instant. tradeoff is cost for pre-warm.
[06:14] Aisha Malik: 2-3 minutes might be too slow for an auth flow spike. we need graceful degradation not catastrophic failures.
[06:21] Jamie Huang: agree. that's why fallthrough to smaller model or returning degraded but safe response is in the plan. also retries with jitter are recommended on client side.
[06:29] Speaker 1: (laugh) yep
[06:32] Leah Kim: any telemetry we'll need to add on our side to help debugging?
[06:36] Carlos Mendez: request ids, end-to-end latency timestamps, and the KV key sharding id would be most helpful. plus the per-request flag whether it hit the KV cache.
[06:47] Aisha Malik: we can add those headers.
[06:50] Jamie Huang: quick sanity check on success criteria — what are we aiming for this sprint? Aisha?
[06:56] Aisha Malik: objective: demonstrate stable 24h steady-state at our expected peak with p95 < 500ms and <0.05% timeouts. if we hit that on hosted we'll consider dedicated.
[07:06] Jamie Huang: good. proposed measurement: run 24h staging test with new batching config and concurrency soft ceilings, produce perf dashboard and key traces.
[07:13] Carlos Mendez: I'll attach the new batching yaml and the heatmap export. also including a sample fallthrough policy file.
[07:19] Tom Bowers: what about SSO / compliance asks — still on track with SOC2 docs? security review next week.
[07:25] Jamie Huang: yes, we sent SOC2 and SAML integration guide last Friday; I'll re-share the link in the follow-up.
[07:30] Leah Kim: perfect. one more question — will quantization affect throughput/latency tradeoffs here?
[07:36] Priya Rao: quantization reduces memory and can improve throughput per-GPU but it can increase variance in latency depending on kernel choices. we can run a quantized pilot on a mirrored test to show effect.
[07:48] Aisha Malik: can we do that in parallel? we have a week to run the 24h test, can Redwood run a quick quantized micro-benchmark?
[07:55] Carlos Mendez: yes we can. will do a short micro-benchmark against your eval set and include token-per-second and p95 numbers.
[08:02] Jamie Huang: summary of agreed actions...
[08:05] Jamie Huang: 1) Redwood: provide batching config, fallthrough policy, KV hit heatmap, and quantization micro-bench by 2027-10-23. 2) Customer: run 24h staging test and deliver logs + eviction metrics by 2027-10-27. 3) Redwood & Customer: sync on canary plan if staging stable by 2027-11-01.
[08:22] Aisha Malik: yep that sounds right.
[08:25] Leah Kim: also Jamie please include cost delta for dedicated pre-warm and committed pool.
[08:29] Jamie Huang: will do.
[08:31] Tom Bowers: any blockers from Redwood infra for adding the extra headers and request ids?
[08:36] Priya Rao: no blockers, it's a standard header pass-through; we'll note how to map them in the docs.
[08:41] Speaker 2: (small pause)
[08:44] Jamie Huang: alright if there are no other questions we'll wrap. thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.
[08:50] Aisha Malik: thanks everyone.
[08:52] Jamie Huang: bye

End of transcript.
